quickAnswer: Boxborough is the 2nd most electric-heated town of the 50 we serve: 29.0% of occupied homes use electricity, and 32.8% of housing units are in multi-unit buildings. Its electricity comes from a municipal utility, so heat pump rebates follow different rules.
body: ## Electric heat in nearly three of ten homes

In the Census Bureau's 2022 American Community Survey (ACS), 628 of Boxborough's 2,166 occupied homes (29.0%) heat with electricity. Only one town on our list heats a larger share of its homes with electricity, and the middle town is at 10.1%. Fuel oil is still the largest single fuel at 809 homes (37.3%), near the middle town's 36.5%, and utility gas heats 574 (26.5%).

Electric heat covers a range, from baseboard to heat pumps, and the Census figure does not say which equipment these homes use. For an owner, the first question is what the equipment is, since that decides what a replacement can look like. Resistance heat is often costly to run, a point worth raising with any contractor, and replacing it with a heat pump can be a direct upgrade path. A house on oil or gas has a different menu.
## Apartment buildings in a small town

Boxborough has 2,196 housing units, yet 699 of them (31.8%) sit in buildings of five or more units, and 720 (32.8%) in multi-unit buildings of any size. That ranks 8th of 50. Single-family detached houses are 1,375 units (62.6%), well under the 76.7% of the middle town. Renters hold 563 households (26.0%), 13th of 50.

Larger buildings can change the work. Heating and cooling in a multi-unit building may mean central plant equipment, rooftop units or individual apartment systems, and the owner or association may control what can be altered. A failed system in a rented unit is urgent, since state rules set minimum indoor temperatures for tenants in winter.
## Young by the standards of the 50 towns

Only 83 Boxborough units (3.8%) were built in 1939 or earlier, the lowest share of all 50 towns (the middle town has 16.6%). The median home dates to 1980, and 270 units (12.3%) have been built since 2010, which ranks 7th. Newer construction usually brings tighter envelopes and more insulation than very old houses, though that varies from building to building. The vacancy rate of 1.4% is 45th of 50.
## Lines on the map

The town is bordered by Littleton to the north, Acton to the east, Stow to the south and Harvard to the west, and Wikipedia says Boxborough was formed from parts of Harvard, Littleton and Stow, and incorporated on February 25, 1783. It covers 10.4 square miles and borders Littleton, Acton, Stow and Harvard. The page also lists historical landmarks and sites on the Freedom Trail, including the Silas Wethebee House (est. 1770) on Hill Road and the Silas Taylor Farm on Flagg Hill. A house of that age can be a very different heating job from a unit in a recent apartment building, and both are part of the town. The population was 5,506 at the 2020 census.
## A municipal electric utility

The Littleton Electric Light & Water Department, a municipal utility, supplies Boxborough. In municipal territory, Mass Save heat pump rebates generally cover only homes heated with natural gas from a Mass Save sponsor, and the utility's own program applies to the rest. With 29.0% of homes already electric, it is worth confirming the rebate path at the start. The [heat pump page](/cities/boxborough/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits) sets out the details.

faq.q: Can a Boxborough homeowner get a Mass Save heat pump rebate?
faq.a: Only in some cases. Because the utility is municipal, Mass Save generally reaches only homes that heat with natural gas from a sponsor, and everyone else is pointed to the municipal utility's own program. Compare both routes for your home, and confirm the current terms at masssave.com before you commit to a purchase.

faq.q: My Boxborough home has electric heat. What are my options?
faq.a: It depends on what the equipment is. With 29.0% of homes heated by electricity, this is a common situation in town. Baseboard or other resistance heat can often be replaced by ductless mini-splits or a ducted heat pump, which both heat and cool. The home's heating load sets the size of the new system.

faq.q: Who pays for heat in a Boxborough rental?
faq.a: Unless the lease says otherwise the landlord covers the heating bill (105 CMR 410.201). In the heating season a rental unit must hold at least 68 F from 7 a.m. to 11 p.m. and 64 F overnight. This is general information, not legal advice. A landlord with a failed system can call (508) 786-8755 at any hour.

faq.q: Do you work on apartment buildings in Boxborough?
faq.a: Mass HVAC does heating, air conditioning, heat pumps, maintenance and indoor air quality work for homes and businesses. With 32.8% of housing units in multi-unit buildings, a building may run central equipment, individual unit systems or both, and an owner or association may need to approve changes.

heating-installation-repair.quickAnswer: Boxborough heats three main ways: fuel oil in 809 occupied homes (37.3%), electricity in 628 (29.0%) and utility gas in 574 (26.5%). Bottled gas serves another 118, so no single fuel dominates and a replacement starts with the house's own fuel.
body: ## Oil, electricity and gas, side by side

The ACS 2022 counts 809 Boxborough homes on oil, 574 on utility gas, 118 on bottled or tank gas (5.4%) and 37 on wood (1.7%). Electricity, at 628 homes, completes the picture. Oil ranks 25th of 50, the middle of the field, and utility gas ranks 35th. With a mix this even, a neighbor's best option may not be yours.
## What each fuel means for a replacement

An oil boiler is a question of tank, chimney and yearly cleaning. Swapping a gas boiler or furnace usually ends with a final inspection, and a licensed plumber or gas fitter has to pull the permit. Propane is treated like gas for permits and adds a tank. An all-electric house has no combustion to replace, and a heat pump is the usual direction; see the [heat pump page](/cities/boxborough/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits).
## Houses from 1960 to 1979

The largest age band here is 807 units (36.7%) built from 1960 to 1979, with 206 more (9.4%) from 1940 to 1959. Heating plants in houses of that age may have been replaced once already. Leaks, rust and a burner that cycles often are signs a unit is wearing out. When a repair bill nears the price of new equipment, a quote for replacement is worth having.
## Rental and apartment heat

About a quarter of Boxborough households rent, and in an apartment building one central boiler may serve many units. When it fails, heat can disappear across the whole building, and for tenants that is both a comfort problem and a legal deadline. Mass HVAC takes emergency calls 24/7 at (508) 786-8755 and gives a free written estimate before work starts.
## Propane and wood

Bottled gas heats 118 homes, 18th of 50, and wood heats 37. The propane group is small, but those homes depend on tank deliveries and a gas permit whenever equipment changes, so a heat pump or a switch to another fuel is a real alternative to weigh.

faq.q: Which professional pulls a gas permit for a new furnace?
faq.a: A licensed plumber or gas fitter, because Massachusetts allows nobody else to pull it. In Boxborough 574 occupied homes heat with utility gas, and a new gas furnace or boiler normally comes with a final inspection. Ask your installer who files the permit before work begins, and ask the town's building department about local steps.

faq.q: Is there after-hours help for an apartment building with no heat?
faq.a: Yes. Call (508) 786-8755 at any hour, for homes and businesses. About a third of Boxborough housing units are in multi-unit buildings, where one dead central boiler can affect many households at once, so tell the dispatcher the building type, the fuel and what failed.

faq.q: Should I replace electric baseboard heat in Boxborough?
faq.a: Electricity heats 628 occupied homes in town, the 2nd highest share of the 50 towns. Baseboard can be replaced by ductless heads or a ducted heat pump, which also cools. Whether that makes sense depends on the house, the electric rate and how much of the home is used, so compare running costs for both options.

air-conditioning-installation-repair.quickAnswer: The town mixes 1,375 detached houses with 699 units in buildings of five or more. Cooling can mean a central system, a rooftop unit or ductless heads, and the type of building often decides which one fits best.
body: ## Houses, townhouses and apartments

According to the ACS 2022, Boxborough has 1,375 single-family detached units (62.6%) and 101 attached townhouses (4.6%). Buildings of five or more units hold 699 units. Cooling a detached house is typically a matter of ducts and an outdoor condenser. Cooling an apartment or townhouse is often limited by where an outdoor unit can go and what the owner or association permits.
## Newer buildings

Boxborough ranks 7th of 50 for homes built since 2010. Newer buildings may come with ductwork, a layout designed for central cooling or both, though that is not guaranteed. Many older homes were built without central air, and for those a ductless mini-split can add cooling without new ducts. Which one fits depends on what the building already has and on how its rooms are arranged.
## Multi-unit work

A property manager or condo board may need a plan covering several units, with equipment that matches across the building. Individual owners may want one system for their own unit, which brings in questions about wall sleeves, balcony space and noise.
## A mixed building, a mixed plan

A single condo owner, a landlord with a few units and a manager of a large complex face different questions: who owns the equipment, who pays for the power, and whether outdoor units can be seen from a window. Those answers can settle the equipment choice before size or brand does.
## Sizing

A unit sized too large cools fast and shuts off before the air is dry. One sized too small runs all afternoon without reaching the set temperature. Sun, insulation and window area all matter, and for an apartment so does the unit's position in the building. Air conditioning work from Mass HVAC covers homes and businesses.

faq.q: Can I put a mini-split in a Boxborough townhouse or condo?
faq.a: Often, yes, but the building's rules and the location of the outdoor unit decide it. Boxborough has 101 attached townhouse units (4.6%) and many units in larger buildings, where an owner or association commonly has a say in what goes on a wall or roof. Check with them first, then plan where the indoor and outdoor parts go.

faq.q: Should a newer Boxborough house get central air or ductless?
faq.a: It depends on whether the house has usable ducts and how the rooms are laid out. A newer house may already have ductwork, though that is not guaranteed. Where ducts are absent or too small for cooling, ductless heads avoid new duct runs, and each head can be set for its own room.

faq.q: Can one cooling system serve a whole apartment building?
faq.a: Some buildings use central or rooftop equipment and others give each unit its own system, so the answer depends on how the building was designed. A property manager may weigh both before choosing, and shared equipment is a decision for the owner or association rather than for one tenant.

heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits.quickAnswer: Boxborough is served by the Littleton Electric Light & Water Department, a municipal utility, so rebates are routed differently than in National Grid towns. Mass Save mainly applies to homes on sponsor natural gas.
body: ## Municipal utility, different rules

The Littleton Electric Light & Water Department serves Boxborough and is municipal. Under the usual arrangement, Mass Save heat pump rebates reach only homes heated with sponsor natural gas, and the municipal utility's own program covers the rest, so ask the utility for its current terms. Fuel decides the path: 574 occupied homes use utility gas, while 809 use oil, 118 bottled gas, 628 electricity and 37 wood. Whether the gas company is a Mass Save sponsor is a separate question, and one to settle before any equipment is ordered.
## Mass Save, briefly

If a home is eligible, Mass Save pays $2,650 per ton in 2026, capped at $8,500, once the house is weatherized. The full terms are on the [main heat pump page](/services/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits).
## Weatherization against Boxborough's age bands

The weatherization test passes homes built in 2000 or later, and Boxborough has 445 such units (20.3%), of which 270 (12.3%) date from 2010 or later. On the other side, 1,096 units (49.9%) predate 1980, led by 807 (36.7%) from 1960 to 1979. For about half the housing stock, an energy assessment would be the usual first step.
## Where a heat pump fits

A heat pump can replace resistance heat and add cooling in the same unit, which is the case for electric baseboard. The Census does not say what equipment the 628 electric homes use. For the 809 oil homes and 118 bottled-gas homes, the comparison is with a combustion system and a tank. The heating load, assessed before quoting, decides how large a system should be.
## Apartments and townhouses

Ductless heads suit a single apartment because each serves one zone, but the outdoor unit usually needs the approval of the owner or association. Noise and refrigerant line routing are worth settling with the building before an order is placed. For the fuel breakdown across the town, see the [Boxborough page](/cities/boxborough).

faq.q: Which rebate applies to my Boxborough heat pump?
faq.a: It depends on how the home is heated. The electric utility is municipal, so a home heating with natural gas from a Mass Save sponsor generally looks to Mass Save, and other homes look to the utility's own program. Ask the Littleton Electric Light & Water Department for its terms, then compare.

faq.q: Can I replace electric baseboard with a mini-split?
faq.a: Usually, because a ductless mini-split needs no ducts, only a small wall opening for each indoor head's refrigerant line. The number of heads depends on the layout, and the home's heating load sets the size. Baseboard in several rooms may call for several heads rather than one.

faq.q: Does the house need weatherizing first?
faq.a: For the Mass Save whole-home rebate, yes: it must be built in 2000 or later, have an assessment recommending under $1,000 of work, or have earlier recommendations completed. With about half of Boxborough's housing built before 1980, many owners would begin with an energy assessment.

hvac-maintenance-tune-ups.quickAnswer: Boxborough has 1,603 owner-occupied households and 563 rented ones, so a tune-up may be for a homeowner or a landlord. The fuel sets the visit: oil wants a burner cleaning, gas a safety check, and heat pumps clean filters and coils.
body: ## Owners and landlords

The ACS 2022 counts 1,603 owner-occupied Boxborough households (74.0%) and 563 rented (26.0%). In an owner-occupied home the household chooses when equipment gets looked at, while in a rental the landlord usually holds the boiler, and a tenant's heat is covered by the sanitary code. A boiler checked before October may be less likely to fail in a cold snap.
## One schedule, several fuels

Boxborough heats with oil, utility gas, electricity and some propane, so no single service visit fits every home. Oil calls for a yearly cleaning, with the nozzle and filter swapped and the combustion tested. Gas calls for a look at the burner, venting and controls. Heat pumps and mini-splits want clean filters and coils and a refrigerant-side check. Baseboard and other electric heat need little, though thermostats and connections are worth a glance.
## Who should do what

Between visits, the occupant can keep filters clean, keep furniture and boxes away from baseboard heaters and the boiler, and report new noises early. A landlord or association can keep a service record for each boiler or rooftop unit so its age and history are known when a failure happens. Boxborough has 30 vacant homes (1.4%), 45th of 50; any property that sits empty through winter still needs heat set to protect the pipes.

- **Late summer:** heating checks.
- **Spring:** cooling checks, outdoor units cleared.
- **Any time:** a new noise, smell or rising bill.
## A median house from 1980

The median Boxborough home was built in 1980, so many boilers and furnaces that came with the house, if still running, are well into old age. A written record of past service makes the repair-or-replace question easier. For repair and replacement, see the [heating page](/cities/boxborough/heating-installation-repair). Mass HVAC offers maintenance for homes and businesses, whatever the fuel.

faq.q: How often should an oil boiler in Boxborough be cleaned?
faq.a: Once a year, ideally before the heating season begins. Oil is the largest single fuel in town, heating 809 occupied homes. A yearly visit cleans the burner, replaces the nozzle and filter and tests combustion, and it can catch a small fault before the first cold snap turns it into a no-heat call.

faq.q: Should a landlord service heating before winter?
faq.a: It helps. A boiler or furnace checked before the heating season is less likely to fail in a cold snap, and tenants are entitled to heat on a set schedule. A written service record also shows the equipment was looked after. This is general information, not legal advice.

faq.q: What does maintenance involve for a mini-split or heat pump?
faq.a: Filters and indoor coils are cleaned, the condensate drain is checked and the refrigerant side is inspected. Each indoor head collects dust like any filter, so a home with several heads has several filters to keep clean. Outdoor units need clearance from snow, leaves and shrubs.

indoor-air-quality.quickAnswer: Boxborough has a large block of late-century housing: 29.8% was built from 1980 to 1999 and 20.3% from 2000 on. Tighter homes can hold moisture and odors, and ventilation, filters and humidity control are the usual levers.
body: ## Tighter buildings, different questions

According to the ACS 2022, 655 Boxborough housing units (29.8%) were built from 1980 to 1999 and 445 (20.3%) from 2000 on. Newer construction is often tighter than older houses, which cuts air leakage but can trap humidity, cooking smells and household chemicals. Planned ventilation, such as exhaust fans or a mechanical ventilation unit, may help. The right choice depends on the building.
## Apartments and shared air

With 699 units in buildings of five or more, shared walls, corridors and ventilation shafts raise their own questions. Smells and moisture can travel between units, and the owner or association may control the ventilation equipment. Where a unit has its own system, filters and cleaning are the occupant's concern.
## Cooking, showers and everyday moisture

In a tight apartment or a recent house, a steamy shower or an hour of cooking raises humidity fast if the fan does not move air outdoors. Windows that fog in winter, a musty closet or peeling paint near a bathroom are common signs. A fan clogged with dust, or one that vents into an attic instead of outdoors, is a frequent culprit.
## Combustion in oil and gas homes

Oil heats 809 occupied homes and utility gas 574, so burners and flues are part of daily life for many households. A yearly check of the burner and venting, plus a working carbon monoxide alarm, covers the basics. Wood heats 37 homes (1.7%), and a wood stove brings smoke and ash questions of its own.
## What to look at

- **Filters:** match the filter to the equipment, and change it on schedule.
- **Humidity:** a very dry or damp home may need a humidifier, a dehumidifier or better ventilation.
- **Fans:** bath and kitchen fans should vent outdoors.
- **Ducts:** where a home has ducts, their condition may affect air quality.

Mass HVAC does indoor air quality work for homes and businesses. If you notice stale air, condensation on windows or a musty smell, note which rooms and when. See the [Boxborough page](/cities/boxborough) for the town overview.

faq.q: Does a newer Boxborough home need mechanical ventilation?
faq.a: It may benefit, since tighter homes hold moisture and odors. The answer depends on the building: its fans, its ducts, how many people live in it and how it is used. A damp bathroom, a stale bedroom or windows that fog in winter would point toward better ventilation before any equipment is chosen.

faq.q: Can an apartment have its own air filtration?
faq.a: Often, within limits set by the building. A portable or in-unit system may help, and the owner or association decides what can be installed in shared systems. A tenant who wants a change to a shared duct or vent should ask the landlord first, in writing.

faq.q: Should I worry about carbon monoxide in a Boxborough apartment?
faq.a: Any unit with a gas or oil appliance, a fireplace or an attached garage can have a carbon monoxide risk, and a working detector is the basic precaution. In a multi-unit building the owner or association usually controls central boilers and flues, so report headaches, soot or a burner smell to the landlord promptly.
